A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MindForge research. Their text, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, with retained material identifiable despite reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original Minecraft experiments on task completion, tech-tree progression, collaboration, generalization and component ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains these empirical results and adds experiments on harder tasks, flexible communication and structured versus unstructured perspective-taking.

M1.justification: v5 adds a flexible communication variant allowing agents to request help before attempting a task, alongside the retained failure-triggered default (Section 5.3 and Appendix A.3). The core BigToM representation, perspective-taking procedure and memory architecture remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v5 extends isolated-task evaluation to mining iron and crafting a wooden pickaxe, and adds a combined dirt-and-wood objective. This expands task-specific communication testing within Minecraft; the existing tech-tree and dirt/wood generalization coverage remains.

E2.justification: v5 evaluates an unstructured two-step perspective-taking alternative inspired by Think Twice (Table 8), which v4 cited but did not evaluate in this comparison. It also compares flexible and default communication variants. Existing Voyager, ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT and PEFT comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments compare fixed versus agent-chosen communication initiation and evaluate Llama 3.1-70B agents with GPT-4 or matched-capability partners across zero to three communication rounds on harder tasks. The existing four-action task protocol and tech-tree evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 substantially expands diagnostic evidence by directly testing structured versus unstructured ToM, sensitivity to communication initiation, and communication-round effects on harder compositional tasks (Tables 4, 6 and 8). These address distinct component and robustness questions beyond v4's retained perspective-taking, memory and post-collaboration analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 24 independent trials for isolated tasks and three-trial tech-tree results with the same uncertainty entries. The new checklist refers to existing practices without adding seeds, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, significance tests or an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and matched appendix values are retained. New Tables 4, 6 and 8 add targeted results; Table 8 reports round-three structured/unstructured success of 45%/41% for pickaxe crafting and 62%/58% for mining iron. New Table 6 reports intermediate Mistral scores of 42% and 45%, differing without explanation from 45% and 50% in the retained communication plot.

T1.justification: Neither version presents original formal theorems or proofs; the Condorcet Jury Theorem remains a qualitative analogy. The added distinction between intentions and actions is conceptual clarification, not changed mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same three principal contributions and claims about cultural learning, improved tech-tree progression, 2.3-fold item collection and communication-driven collaborative gains. New experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v5 qualifies the intention/action equivalence as implementation-specific and interprets the flexible-protocol results as evidence of independence from a particular initiation design. It also removes v4's explicit limitation that small-model hallucinations can disrupt causal representations and perspective-taking.

D1.justification: The new checklist states that supplementary materials contain the full experimental code and README instructions, and discloses that the human expert was an author. Actual code accessibility cannot be verified from these PDFs. Existing prompts, API providers, retrieval settings and fine-tuning details are retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds comparisons with ExpeL, CLIN, DEPS, ADaPT and SSO in a new single-agent related-work paragraph, sharpens its distinction from CoELA and COMBO, and adds a citation concerning unrealized intentions. The established research positioning otherwise remains.

P1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 are retitled and rewritten to distinguish self-modeling from partner ToM. Appendices regroup results, ablations and implementation details; acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist are added, while the standalone limitations section is removed. Most remaining prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v5 adds three tables and a MindForge column in Table 1 that redisplays scores already present in v4's Table 2. It moves the belief diagram from appendix Figure 8 to main-text Figure 3, relocates other displays and relabels the communication-flow diagram. The overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: The new structured-ToM and communication-protocol controls make central design choices better supported, while the revised method explanation clarifies self-modeling versus partner perspective-taking. These provide a modest net improvement. Benefits are tempered by unchanged uncertainty reporting, removal of the explicit hallucination caveat, and the unexplained Mistral-score disagreement between new Table 6 and retained Figure 5.
